entities.summary: The Khanqah-e-Moula, also known as Shah-e-Hamadan Masjid and the Khanqah, is a Sunni mosque located in the Old City of Srinagar, in the Indian-administered union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. Situated on the right bank of the river Jhelum between the Fateh Kadal and Zaina Kadal bridges, it was built in 1395 CE, and was commissioned by Sultan Sikandar in memory of Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani. It is held to be the first khanqah — mosques associated with specific saints — in the Kashmir Valley. It is one of the best examples of Kashmiri wooden architecture, and is decorated with papier mache. Khanqah-e-Moula is a mosque in Asia, established in 1395. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Khanqah-e-Moula is a significant regional landmark in Kashmir Valley, showcasing unique wooden architecture and papier mache decorations. Its construction in 1395 CE by Sultan Sikandar in memory of Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani highlights the importance of Sufi shrines in South Asian history.
